items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a statewide
advanced care planning campaign to promote public awareness of hospice and
palliative care services
items.lawCode: Amd §207, rpld §207 sub 1 ¶(h), Pub Health L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8205

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a
statewide advanced care planning campaign to promote public awareness of
hospice and palliative care services

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to create a public education campaign
to inform the public about the importance of advance care planning and
to raise awareness of hospice and palliative care services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 4010 of the public health law and requires that
the commissioner establish a statewide advanced care planning campaign.
The campaign will promote public awareness of hospice and palliative
care services, inform the public of the importance of advanced care
planning, and educate individuals on the tools available to ensure their
health care decisions are honored.

Section 2 of this bill is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York State is consistently ranked at the bottom of hospice and
palliative care utilization metrics. One of the most glaring issues
leading to this chronic underutilization of vital services is a lack of
public awareness and education on hospice and palliative care.

This gap in knowledge leaves many individuals unprepared should they
become seriously ill or a develop life-limiting illness, leaving fami-
lies struggling to ascertain their loved one's values and desires for
end-of-life care. It also leads to unnecessary medical interventions and
rehospitalizations which could have been avoided if individuals had the
foresight to communicate their desires in advance. A statewide advanced
care planning campaign would promote public awareness and education
about advanced care planning tools and the benefits and availability of
hospice and palliative care services. This campaign would also ensure
more equitable distribution of hospice and palliative care services, as
there are currently alarming racial disparities in the utilization of
hospice and palliative care. Of the 30% of New Yorkers who utilized
hospice for end-of-life care, only 9% were Black, 3% Hispanic, and 2%,
Asian. Public perception of hospice and palliative care in communities
of color remains a roadblock to access, along with language barriers and
culturally-based apprehension regarding the cessation of curative treat-
ment. An inclusive and culturally competent public awareness campaign
would help close disparity gaps in care and ensure all New Yorkers have
access to critical end-of-life services.

This bill would require the Department of Health develop and implement a
statewide campaign to inform the public of the importance of advance
care planning and improve awareness and utilization of hospice and
palliative care services. Mediums for interventions may include media,
social media, material distribution, state-wide education of NYS employ-
ees, long-term care facilities, and other providers.
 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.
